key_insight: AI needs to move beyond short-horizon wins (like AlphaGo) toward models and training paradigms that support robust, temporally-extended strategic planning across complex tasks.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between milestone, narrow-domain successes and the challenge of building models that reliably plan and act over long time scales in realistic, multi-step environments.
method: Synthesis of the decade of progress since AlphaGo, identifying techniques (e.g., self-play, planning, world models) that enabled breakthrough performance.
Articulates model-level priorities for the ‘long game’: hierarchical/temporal abstraction, explicit world models and memory, and objective formulations that reward long-term outcomes.
Proposes evaluation and research directions: long-horizon benchmarks, training regimes for temporal credit assignment, and robustness/safety checks for extended behavior.
impact: Shifts practitioner focus from short-term metric gains to architectures, training pipelines, and evaluations that capture and validate long-horizon reasoning—essential for real-world, strategic AI applications.
visual_elements: Timeline: AlphaGo → key milestones over the last decade → current long-horizon focus
Diagram of a hierarchical planner/world model (short-term controller nested in long-term planner)
Chart: model performance (or reliability) versus planning horizon to show diminishing returns without long-horizon design
Research agenda panel: benchmarks, training techniques, evaluation & safety icons
